content.text:
terraria's settings live in the game's own config files on this server, so the ordinary approach is the right one: browse_files from the top of the data directory to find the file that holds the setting, read_file to see it, edit_file to change just that piece, then restart to apply it. Nothing is hidden in the environment on this game, so what you find in those files is the whole picture.

There is no supported way to install mods on terraria through this bot — no registry is wired up for it, so there is nothing to search and nothing to write. Say so plainly. Don't improvise an install by hand through the file tools: anything put there that way is outside everything that would otherwise check it and put it back. If someone wants mods on this game, escalate it as a feature request.

content.text:
I found the problem and fixed it. The server's back up and is reading your settings again.

**What was wrong:** When you edited the main settings file (`config/config.json`), an extra comma ended up after the last setting on line 156 (`"ApplicationRestTokens": {},`). That one comma made the whole file invalid, so the server rejected it on startup. The log showed `parse error: Expected another key-value pair at line 157`. The server kept running, but it wasn't using your settings, which is why your changes weren't showing up.

**What I did:**
1. Removed the extra comma and checked that the file is valid.
2. Restarted the server. Nobody was online, so no one got disconnected.
3. Checked the new startup log. The error is gone and the server started normally.

**Your spawn protection settings now:**
- `"SpawnProtectionRadius": 25` (your increase is in)
- `"SpawnProtection": false`, which means spawn protection is **switched off**. The bigger radius won't do anything while it's off. If you want spawn protected, tell me and I'll set it to `true` and restart.

**Also:** The startup log still shows a `/setup 8131033` code. That means the first-time admin setup was never finished. Until you join the game and run that command, nobody on the server has admin rights.

If you edit the file by hand again, check that the last setting in each `{ }` block has no comma after it. Otherwise you can just ask me to make the change.
